title: 🐳 How to Dockerize a Spring Boot Application?
excerpt: Different environments, missing dependencies, and configuration issues can cause problems.
body:
ㅤ
📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 11
ㅤ
Have you ever built an application that works perfectly on your computer but fails on another machine? 🤔

Different environments, missing dependencies, and configuration issues can cause problems.

That's where Docker comes in!

Let's understand it with a Spring Boot example. 👇
ㅤ
1️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘀 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗿? 🐳

Docker is a platform that packages applications and their dependencies into containers.

A container provides a consistent environment for running an application.

✅ Consistent environments
✅ Easier deployment
✅ Application isolation
✅ Portable across supported systems
ㅤ
2️⃣ 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗿 𝗜𝗺𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝘃𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿 📦

These two concepts are important:

🔹 Docker Image
A packaged template containing the application and everything needed to run it.

🔹 Docker Container
A running instance of a Docker image.

💡 Image = Blueprint
💡 Container = Running application
ㅤ
3️⃣ 𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗶𝗹𝗲 ⚙️

A Dockerfile contains instructions for building an image.

Example:

FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre

WORKDIR /app

COPY target/app.jar app.jar

EXPOSE 8080

ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]

This packages a pre-built Spring Boot JAR with a Java runtime.

The JAR must be built before creating the image.
ㅤ
4️⃣ 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝘂𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿 🚀

Build the Docker image:

docker build -t springboot-app .

Run the container:

docker run -p 8080:8080 springboot-app

Now the application can be accessed through:

http://localhost:8080

Assuming the application starts successfully on port 8080.
ㅤ
5️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲? 🔗

Real applications often require multiple services.

For example:

☕ Spring Boot — Backend API
🐘 PostgreSQL — Database
⚡ Redis — Caching

Docker Compose helps define and run these services together using a YAML configuration.

Example command:

docker compose up -d
ㅤ
6️⃣ 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗿 𝘃𝘀 𝗩𝗶𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗲 🖥️

🔹 Docker Container
Shares the host kernel and isolates application processes.

🔹 Virtual Machine
Runs a separate guest operating system using virtualization.

Containers are generally more lightweight than full virtual machines.
ㅤ
💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

Docker isn't just about running applications inside containers.

It helps developers create consistent environments, simplify deployments, and manage dependencies.

Understanding Docker is a valuable skill when building modern backend applications.
